cleanIntro: This is the same Pedersoli side-by-side smooth bore chapter as the percussion gun, pages 22 to 26, plus one section that exists only for you: SPECIAL NOTES FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING FLINT LOCKS on page 25. Everything at the front of the gun — wedges, hook breech, chromed bores, choke tubes — is identical. Everything at the back is not. You have vents instead of nipples, pans and frizzens instead of caps, and one hazard the percussion gun does not have at all: the flash from the first barrel can set off the second. Read the flintlock section as a set of rules about the gun, not as trivia about the period.

steps.title: Both barrels unloaded, both pans empty, muzzles safe
steps.action: Prove both barrels empty with the ramrod against your own load marks, then check both pans are dry and unprimed and both frizzens are open. A flintlock with a primed pan is a loaded gun even with the frizzen closed, and on a double you have two of them. Pedersoli opens the side-by-side chapter with this instruction and everything after it assumes you did it.
steps.prose: Brush the pans out rather than blowing them — priming powder blown back into a lock finds its way under the frizzen spring.
steps.quote: WARNING: BEFORE PROCEEDING ALWAYS MAKE SURE THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED AND POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Loading and shooting instructions for side by side muzzle loading smooth bore shotguns, p.22
steps.warn: Both barrels. Both pans. Both frizzens open.

steps.title: FLINTLOCK ONLY — the second barrel can be lit by the first
steps.action: This is the hazard that belongs to your gun and not to the percussion version. With both barrels loaded and both pans primed, the flame that leaves the first lock can reach across and ignite the second pan, firing a barrel you never intended to fire. Pedersoli's remedy is procedural, not mechanical: leave the second lock's pan unprimed while you fire the first barrel, and prime it only afterwards.
steps.prose: This is the flintlock equivalent of the percussion rule about one cap at a time, and it is enforced the same way — by what you put in the pan, not by the safety.
steps.quote: To avoid this risk, we recommend leaving the pan of the second lock unprimed, while firing the first barrel.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Special notes for side by side muzzle loading flint locks, p.25
steps.warn: Prime one lock at a time. Never both.

steps.title: Never drop a cock on an empty jaw
steps.action: When you let the cocks down, control them with your thumb onto a closed frizzen with a flint fitted — never let one fall with an empty jaw. On a flintlock the frizzen face is a hardened striking surface and the flint is what is meant to hit it; steel jaws landing on it directly bruise the face and ruin the spark for good. Pedersoli states the rule in the same breath as the percussion nipple rule.
steps.prose: A gouged frizzen face throws sparks sideways instead of down into the pan, and no amount of knapping fixes it.
steps.caution: Flint fitted, frizzen closed, thumb on the cock. Every time.
steps.quote: 7) Never let the hammer on a percussion firearm fall without a cap on nipple or it will damage the nipple. On a flintlock arm, never let the hammer fall on the frizzen without a flint in the hammer.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Important cautions for muzzle loading shooting, point 7, p.12

steps.title: Ramrod out, then the wedges
steps.action: Pull the ramrod clear of its thimbles before anything else — the barrels will not lift with it in place and levering against a trapped rod splits the forend. Then retract the wedge or wedges that pass through the stock and the barrel lugs, driving them out the way they went in. They are a light interference fit and should move under a brass or nylon drift with hand pressure, not hammer blows.
steps.prose: The side-by-side is one of Pedersoli's hook-breech guns, so there is no tang screw to undo first.
steps.caution: A steel drift on a wedge marks the stock inlet. Use brass or nylon.
steps.quote: 2c) For the guns of the seconds group, the barrel is fixed to the stock with wedges. Once removed the ramrod, retract the wedge or wedges, handle the barrel at the muzzle and rotate towards the height, the lug will disengage from its seat.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — How to remove the barrel from stock, point 2c, p.20

steps.title: Lift the barrels off the hook
steps.action: With the wedges out, take the barrels at the muzzle and rotate them upward until the hook at the breech disengages from its seat in the tang. The whole barrel assembly then comes free of the stock in one piece. Lift rather than pull forward — the hook is a rotating joint, and dragging it out sideways bruises both the hook and the seat it has to index against for the life of the gun.
steps.prose: You are now holding two chromed smooth bores with a vent in the side of each breech instead of a drum and nipple.
steps.quote: handle the barrel at the muzzle and rotate towards the height, the lug will disengage from its seat.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — How to remove the barrel from stock, point 2c, p.20

steps.title: Vents out — and that is where the strip stops
steps.action: Take the vent liner out of each barrel so hot water can flow straight through the flash hole rather than dead-ending against it. Pedersoli's cleaning instruction names the vent as the flintlock equivalent of the percussion nipple, and it is the only part of this shotgun's breech you are asked to remove. The breech plug behind it does not come out on a side-by-side, even though the same booklet gives a breech-plug removal procedure for single-shot guns on page 21.
steps.prose: The maker also notes the work is easier if the breech end of the barrel sits in hot water for a few minutes first — heat and water do most of the loosening.
steps.quote: Flintlock rifles or pistols: remove the vent. The work can be easier leaving the breech plug barrel into hot water for some minutes.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Cleaning instructions for single shot muzzle loading guns, Cleaning, p.21
steps.warn: On the side by side: ATTENTION: the breech plug CANNOT BE REMOVED.

steps.title: PROHIBITED — the drum and the breech plug do not come out
steps.action: If a wad or a shot charge is stuck part-way down a bore, do not open the back of the barrel to push it out. Pedersoli forbids that for every gun in this booklet without exception. The way out is a screw-tip bullet puller of the correct calibre worked from the muzzle, with black powder solvent poured down to soften the fouling holding it. Opening the breech instead is how a shotgun barrel gets scrapped and a shooter gets hurt.
steps.prose: The shotgun chapter repeats the same limit in its own words in the cleaning section: the breech plug cannot be removed.
steps.quote: UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES SHOULD THE INDIVIDUAL ATTEMPT TO REMOVE THE PERCUSSION DRUM OR BREECH PLUG FROM THE FIREARM.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Important cautions for muzzle loading shooting, point 17, p.12
steps.warn: This prohibition bars a teardown. It does NOT bar cleaning — the whole cleaning sequence below is done with the breech plug in place.

steps.title: Hot soapy water through both bores, same day
steps.action: Black powder fouling is corrosive and hygroscopic and it starts on the steel within hours, so this happens on the day, not at the weekend. Stand the breech ends in hot water with a black powder detergent and work a tight patch or bristle brush down each bore in turn; water draws in and out through the open vent seats as you stroke. Do both barrels, and wipe the ribs, the lock plates and the underside where fouling hides.
steps.prose: Pedersoli notes the shotgun bores are chromed and then sends you to the single-shot cleaning procedure unchanged.
steps.aside: 12f) Our shotguns have chromed barrel bores, however the same procedures seen at point 2c and at “CLEANING” of section “CLEANING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SINGLE SHOT MUZZLE LOADING GUNS” in this booklet, are to be followed.
steps.quote: Scrub bore with hot soapy water or in hot water with specific detergent (item USA 487) and wipe all powder fouling from all other metallic parts too.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Cleaning instructions for single shot muzzle loading guns, Cleaning, p.21

steps.title: Flush hot, dry hot, oil as it cools
steps.action: Rinse both bores with the hottest clean water available so the soap goes out with it, then dry them at once with fresh patches while the steel is still hot — residual heat drives moisture out of the vent seats and the pan recesses where a patch cannot reach. Oil the bores and every metal surface as soon as they cool. Leaving flintlock barrels to cool wet pits them at the breech, and the pan and frizzen rust faster than the bore does.
steps.prose: Hot metal dries itself. Cold metal keeps a film of water exactly where you cannot see it.
steps.caution: Oil the barrel lightly as soon as it cools inside and out. Apply a coat of oil to all metallic parts too.
steps.quote: Dry barrel and all metallic parts rapidly with fresh patches while they are still hot.
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Cleaning instructions for single shot muzzle loading guns, Cleaning, p.21

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The barrels are off the stock, both vents are out, both bores are clean, dry and oiled, and the breech plugs have never moved. That is the whole of the strip Pedersoli publishes for a side-by-side flintlock shotgun. Deep Clean covers the lock geometry check and the flint knapping procedure that belong to this gun alone, plus the choke tubes if yours is fitted for them.
steps.prose: Refit the vents before the barrels go back so you are not fighting them in the stock.
steps.quote: Replace the nipple (on percussion models), or vent (on flintlock models).
steps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Cleaning instructions for single shot muzzle loading guns, Cleaning, p.21

deepSteps.title: FLINTLOCK ONLY — check both locks sit parallel at half cock
deepSteps.action: With both barrels unloaded, bring both cocks to half cock and close both frizzens, then look along the locks. Every component should be perfectly parallel; if a flint is touching its frizzen the frizzen sits slightly open, and a frizzen that is not closed does not hold priming powder in the pan. This is a geometry check Pedersoli asks for specifically on the side-by-side, because the two locks have to behave identically for the capping-order rule above to work.
deepSteps.prose: A frizzen held ajar by a proud flint also dumps priming into the lock mortise, which is where flintlock fouling starts.
deepSteps.caution: Both barrels unloaded before either cock is moved.
deepSteps.quote: Also, ensure that when both hammers are in the half cock position and the frizzens are closed, that all components should be perfectly parallel.
deepSteps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Special notes for side by side muzzle loading flint locks, p.25

deepSteps.title: FLINTLOCK ONLY — knap the flint with a non-ferritic hammer
deepSteps.action: If a flint stands proud enough to touch the frizzen, the fix is to knap it back rather than to reset the jaws and hope. Use a small hammer of non-ferritic material — Pedersoli's own flintlock tool set USA 513 carries one — and take small chips off the striking edge. Steel on flint throws hot fragments and can spark against a lock you are working over, which is precisely why the maker specifies the material.
deepSteps.prose: Knapping restores the sharp edge that scrapes the frizzen. A rounded flint scrapes without cutting and gives a shower of sparks that goes nowhere.
deepSteps.quote: The solution is to knap the flint with a small hammer, of non-ferritic material such as in our Flintlock tool set USA 513. This operation must be performed with both barrels unloaded and placed in safe position.
deepSteps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Special notes for side by side muzzle loading flint locks, p.25
deepSteps.warn: WARNING: Use protection for the eyes and ears.

deepSteps.title: Vent seats and pans
deepSteps.action: With the vents out, clear each flash hole and its seat with a pick and solvent so both barrels light at the same speed, then scrub the pans and the undersides of the frizzens where scale builds up. Refit the vents snug and stop — Pedersoli's warning about excessive force on breech-end threads applies to the vent as much as to a nipple, and a stripped vent thread in a shotgun barrel is not a field repair.
deepSteps.prose: Unequal flash holes are the usual reason one lock of a double feels slower than the other.
deepSteps.quote: When reassembling the drum and the nipple do not apply an excessive strength, or you may break the parts.
deepSteps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — How to remove the breech plug from barrel, p.21
deepSteps.warn: Clean the vent seat. Do not touch the breech plug.

deepSteps.title: Choke tubes, if your shotgun takes them
deepSteps.action: A Pedersoli side-by-side may be threaded for interchangeable chokes. Take each tube out, clean the muzzle threads and the tube threads, grease them lightly and run the tube back until properly tight — a tube that backs out under recoil damages the muzzle and the tube together. Re-check them part way through a long day rather than assuming they stayed put; that is the maker's own advice.
deepSteps.prose: Never change a tube on a loaded gun: on a muzzleloader that means an unproved bore pointing at your hands while you work at the muzzle.
deepSteps.caution: We do not recommend chokes tighter than improved-cylinder for steel shot.
deepSteps.quote: Never change choke tubes on a loaded firearm.
deepSteps.cite: MUZZLELOADING GUNS — OWNER'S MANUAL — LOADING AND SHOOTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR SIDE BY SIDE MUZZLE LOADING SMOOTH BORE SHOTGUNS — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Double barrel shotgun with interchangeable choke tubes, p.26

cleaning.name: BARRELS AND BORES
tasks: Clean the same day you shoot — black powder fouling is corrosive
Vents out of both barrels before water goes near them; a few minutes in hot water first makes it easier
Hot soapy water or hot water with black powder detergent (item USA 487) through both bores
Flush with the hottest clean water available to carry the soap out
Dry both bores and every metal part with fresh patches WHILE STILL HOT
Oil the bores and all metal as soon as they cool

cleaning.name: IGNITION — FLINTLOCK
tasks: Clear both flash holes and vent seats; refit the vents snug, never forced
Scrub the pans and the frizzen undersides
Check both locks sit perfectly parallel at half cock with the frizzens closed
Knap a proud flint with a NON-FERRITIC hammer, both barrels unloaded, eyes and ears protected
PROHIBITED: do not remove the drum or the breech plug from the firearm
Never let a cock fall on a frizzen with no flint in the jaws

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBES (IF FITTED)
tasks: Never change tubes on a loaded firearm
Clean and lightly grease the muzzle and tube threads
Make sure the tube is properly tightened before shooting, and re-check during a long session
No choke tighter than improved cylinder with steel shot

cleaning.name: STOCK AND FURNITURE
tasks: Wipe fouling from both lock plates, cocks and the tang
Check the barrel channel and wedge holes are dry before the barrels go back

reassembly: Refit both vents, snug only — excessive force breaks the parts.
Hook the barrel breech into the tang and confirm it seats properly before the barrels come down.
Lower the barrels into the stock channel — do not force barrel into stock.
The barrels must fit with a minimal amount of tension so the wedges are held in.
Gently insert the wedges RIGHT TO LEFT, then refit the ramrod.
fncheck: With both vents fitted and both pans empty, bring each cock to half cock and to full cock one lock at a time and confirm it holds at both. Close both frizzens with the cocks at half cock and sight along them: everything should be perfectly parallel, with no flint touching a frizzen and no frizzen standing ajar. Check the barrels sit hard in the stock with the wedges home and no gap at the tang, and that the ramrod runs freely. Snap each lock on an empty pan and watch where the sparks land — they should fall into the pan, not past it.
